title: An affine-space cell in a Borel quotient
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G$ be a smooth connected affine $F$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-connected-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $B\subseteq G$ be a Borel subgroup, meaning a maximal smooth connected solvable closed subgroup, where solvable means that iterating the scheme-theoretic derived subgroup eventually gives the trivial group; the derived subgroup is the smallest closed subgroup through which the commutator morphism factors. Let $Q$ represent the fppf sheaf quotient $G/B$ (the sheafification of $A\mapsto G(A)/B(A)$ for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings of commutative $F$-algebras). There exist an integer $d\geq0$ and a dense open immersion $j:\mathbf A^d_F\hookrightarrow Q$ [def-weil-open-immersion], [def-sbc-affine-space]. Dense means that the topological closure of the image is all of $Q$. The case $G=B$, with $d=0$, is included.

source.place: Lemma 18.21, proof, printed p.392: the open subvariety U isomorphic to affine n-space; it invokes Proposition 13.52 and the proof of Theorem 17.65, printed p.374. The standing group is split connected, automatic over F; no reductivity hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-borel-quotient-affine-cell] to the given $F,G,B,Q$. Its field, smoothness, connectedness, affineness and finite-type hypotheses are exactly those in the statement; its Borel definition and fppf quotient are the same ones. It supplies $n\geq0$, a dense open subscheme $U\subseteq Q$, and an $F$-isomorphism $h:U\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Spec}F[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$. Only this cell clause is needed; no reductivity assumption is introduced.

source.place: Lemma 18.21, proof, printed p.392; Proposition 13.52, printed p.275, and proof of Theorem 17.65, printed p.374.

proof.text: Put $d=n$. By the affine-base description in [def-sbc-affine-space], identify $\mathbf A_F^d$ with $\operatorname{Spec}F[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$. Define $j$ to be this identification followed by $h^{-1}$ and $U\hookrightarrow Q$. It identifies its source isomorphically with the open subscheme $U$, hence is an open immersion by [def-weil-open-immersion]. Its topological image is exactly $U$, whose closure is all of $Q$ by step 1. Thus $j$ is dense.

source.place: Lemma 18.21, proof, printed p.392; Proposition 13.52, printed p.275, and proof of Theorem 17.65, printed p.374.

proof.text: For the explicit case $G=B$, every quotient set $G(A)/B(A)$ is a singleton, so its sheafification is the terminal fppf sheaf. Thus its representing $F$-scheme $Q$ is $\operatorname{Spec}F$: both represent the functor with one element on every test algebra, and the mutually unique maps are inverse. Take $d=0$ and the resulting isomorphism $j:\mathbf A_F^0=\operatorname{Spec}F\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$ using [def-sbc-affine-space]. This is an open immersion by [def-weil-open-immersion], with image all of $Q$.

source.place: Lemma 18.21, proof, printed p.392; zero-dimensional case from the quotient and affine-space definitions.
